answers.comment: The 4 are the direct implementers (Handler, HandlerWrapper, and two test classes in LoggerTest.php); true as written. It does not say that the ~100 concrete handlers reach HandlerInterface only transitively (via Handler/AbstractHandler) so an agent asking 'what implements HandlerInterface' gets 4, not the handler family, with no note that the answer is direct-only.

findings: Calls on an object whose class overrides a method are bound to the base-class method (Handler::handleBatch instead of MailHandler/ElasticaHandler::handleBatch; Handler::close instead of SocketHandler::close): 3 of 30 sampled high-confidence edges are this wrong override, with no indication of the override.

Low-confidence name-only guesses bind PHPUnit mock-builder ->with(...) calls to the repository's LogRecord::with (4 of 30 low edges); an anonymous-class method boom() is bound to a named class's static boom() (1 of 30).

Fluent chains are only partly followed: in SlackRecord's constructor 6 of the 8 chained calls (setUsername, useAttachment, useShortAttachment, includeContextAndExtra, excludeFields, setFormatter) stay 'ambiguous' and produce no edge; $handler->isHandling() in Logger::addRecord also has no edge.

find_implementations name=HandlerInterface returns only the 4 direct implementers and does not state that it is direct-only, so the answer understates the implementing family (~100 handler classes via Handler/AbstractHandler).

Most hierarchy edges are medium/low (215 of 242) although the supertype is declared in the same namespace and the targets are all right; the answers then carry 'mixed/weak' verdicts that are more pessimistic than the facts.
Definitions are exact for the five files (130/130, no spurious, no line off by an attribute); parsing is clean (250/250).
Sampled call edges are mostly test-file edges (about 80%), so precision on library code alone is not what these samples measure.
